Full Effect Desc:Automatically sample adjacent vacuum amoebas. Gain a little data and supplies. Quickly get rid of infestations.

Full Effect Desc:Aids in artifact identification by reducing the number of incorrect choices by 2.
Full Effect Desc:Allows asteroid mining and increases the chance (+30%) it will produce something valuable.

Full Effect Desc:Repairs a small percentage of your ship's hull every 3 turns, and helps repair a damaged shuttle.

Full Effect Desc:Increases the amount of cargo your ship can carry by 10. Can be installed multiple times.
Full Effect Desc:Automatically retrieves nearby cargo in space.
Full Effect Desc:+3 turns duration for tactical cloaks, and 30% less cool down and supply use for all cloaks.
Full Effect Desc:A finely tuned scanner that reveals the location of any Firaxughinian datapads.
Full Effect Desc:50% chance of blocking an enemy's call for help, and a 50% chance that kills won't damage your reputation.
Full Effect Desc:Converts commodities found into supplies. Eats asteroids and nebula. No effect on planets or stations. Commodities thrown into reactor yield double supplies.

Full Effect Desc:Reduces the damage and duration of any negative 'status effect' (like poisoned or slowed) by half. Also increases your suit's environmental resistance by 10 or 10%, whichever is higher.
Full Effect Desc:Allows your ship to travel through previously impassible stars and planets.
Full Effect Desc:Increases (doubles!) the amount of credits received from any 'credits' item found. Does not affect item prices.
Full Effect Desc:Luxury living space for 20 additional crew. Also raises the away team maximum size by 2.
Full Effect Desc:Increases the rate at which you earn positive reputation with all alien species, by +100% per level.
Full Effect Desc:Experimental device used to modify stellar spectra. No practical applications found.
Full Effect Desc:Allows docking at any station or embassy, regardless of that race's opinion of you... For a price!
Full Effect Desc:Allows safe travel through ion storms.
Full Effect Desc:Allows your ship to fly near black holes without taking damage. Also allows travel above gas giant planets.
Full Effect Desc:Increases the amount of credits you receive from selling items in the pawn shop by +25%. Does not affect commodity prices.
Full Effect Desc:Allows the away team to effectively see through obstacles like trees, mountains, and walls, up to a distance of 3 tiles.
Full Effect Desc:Protects your ship's systems. Has a [level]% chance to negate a cooldown-inducing critical hit or the shock from an ion storm.
Full Effect Desc:Allows the away team to cross acid. Protects against corrosive effects and attacks.
Full Effect Desc:Increases damage done by the away team's ranged weapons by +20%.
Full Effect Desc:Place where the crew can enjoy artificial environments. Decreases the cost of hiring new personnel by half!
Full Effect Desc:Reduces the chances of contracting diseases, constantly works to cure them, and will suggest a method of curing disease with rare plants. Half as effective against mutated diseases.
Full Effect Desc:Increases the damage done by all your ship's weapons by 15%.
Full Effect Desc:Not only protects from ion storms, but absorbs them, and uses the power to charge your shields.
Full Effect Desc:Increases the total number of crew you can hire by 10, and raises the maximum away team size by 1.
Full Effect Desc:Boosts the range of your ship's sensors by 1.
Full Effect Desc:Improves the quality (tech level) of all crafted components by 15%.
Full Effect Desc:Injured officers heal 2 more per turn. Also helps cure diseases faster.
Full Effect Desc:Safely clear away minefields 100% of the time. Also increases mine detection range.
Full Effect Desc:Makes monsters much more likely to flee from the away team.
Full Effect Desc:Allows the away team to enter mountain tiles, which provide cover and a sight range boost.
Full Effect Desc:As your ship moves, it will create nebula in its wake.
Full Effect Desc:Decreases the damage of your ship weapons by 30%. Also increases the chance of creating a shipwreck by 30%.
Full Effect Desc:Grants +1 bonus XP each time an officer earns more than 1 XP.
Full Effect Desc:Hides up to 30 cargo units of contraband goods and illegal weapons from scanners. Can be installed multiple times.
Full Effect Desc:Increases the amount of oxygen carried by your away teams by +75.
Full Effect Desc:Distorts the electromagnetic output of your ship, effectively increasing your evasion and reducing incoming attack damage by 15%.
Full Effect Desc:Operates like a melee weapon for your ship: bump to attack! This will end your turn.
Full Effect Desc:Reduces the range at which monsters will detect the away team by 2 tiles.
Full Effect Desc:Gain +1 fame for all your heroic actions.
Full Effect Desc:Allows travel into a black hole, but it still sounds like suicide...
Full Effect Desc:You can detect quest items at a distance and see them even in unrevealed tiles.
Full Effect Desc:Allows your ship to safely travel through radiation belts, where few will follow.
Full Effect Desc:Allows your ship to absorb nebula, and use the raw material as fuel (supplies). An effect level of 300+ will also absorb dark nebula.
Full Effect Desc:Increases the amount of resources found on away missions to planets.
Full Effect Desc:Slowly builds a cybernetic workforce to crew your ship.
Full Effect Desc:Allows asteroid mining. Allows your ship to enter dense asteroids and disperse them. May also reveal mine-able asteroids.
Full Effect Desc:Increases the amount of data gathered from all sources by at least 1 but sometimes a lot more.
Full Effect Desc:Your away team will slowly regain lost HP. Also aids in repairing suit punctures.
Full Effect Desc:Regenerates your shields +5% per turn, in addition to the normal rate, and regardless of cooldown.
Full Effect Desc:Increases the base strength of your shields by 30%, allowing them to absorb more damage.
Full Effect Desc:Increases your ship's speed by 15, possibly giving you more moves while your enemies remain still.
Full Effect Desc:Reduces the range at which other ships can detect you by 1 tile.  Also reduces the range enemies can decloak your ship, to a minimum of 1 (adjacent).
Full Effect Desc:Allows your ship to store 2000 more supplies so you don't have to re-fuel as often. Can be installed multiple times.
Full Effect Desc:Decreases the overall supply use of your ship by 5 each turn. Depending on supply usage and other skills, it is possible to generate supplies each turn!

Full Effect Desc:Allow the away team to safely cross lava. At level 2, negates 'burn' status effects.
Full Effect Desc:Automatically reveals any space stations and warp points in the sector.
Full Effect Desc:With the VTOL, your shuttle will choose a new spot each time it lands on a planet.

Full Effect Desc:Cuts the cooldown time of your warp drive in half. Also extends the range of your warp drive by 2 sectors.
Full Effect Desc:The away team will automatically pick up all nearby items.
Full Effect Desc:Allows the away team to cross water (or any other non-damaging liquid).

Full Effect Desc:Fly over stars to gather supplies directly from stellar output.

Full Effect Desc:Reduces shuttle cooldown time by 4. Increases away mission supply cost.
Full Effect Desc:Allows the away team to walk on the hull of shipwrecks, if you can find a way outside.

Full Effect Desc:Slowly restores the ammunition of any grenade item. It is installed on the ship, but also functions on away missions.
Full Effect Desc:"Trader Radio". Get price, shortage, and surplus information even from unexplored sectors.

Full Effect Desc:On away missions, creatures that are beyond your line-of-sight will appear as red dots.
Full Effect Desc:Every time you shoot another ship, there is a 50% chance that it will drop something valuable.
Full Effect Desc:When hailing other vessels, you have a much higher chance of getting a positive outcome (and a reputation increase).

Full Effect Desc:Away Team takes 25% less damage. This applies to the vast majority of types and sources of damage.
Full Effect Desc:Fit more commodities in your cargo hold (50% more commodities per unit of cargo space, or at least +1 more).

Full Effect Desc:All cannon-type ship weapons get +1 range.
Full Effect Desc:Ship beam weapons inflict 33% more damage.

Full Effect Desc:Get 5x as many supplies from anything burned in the reactor.

Full Effect Desc:Cross all planetary surface terrain, even liquid metal. Useless in caves or on high-gravity planets.
Full Effect Desc:Employs a lossy subspace matter stream to sell almost anything, instantly, at half its value.
Full Effect Desc:Cuts all environmental damage in half.
Full Effect Desc:Returns 50% of incoming melee damage, reducing harm to the away team and hurting their attackers.

Be Devious?: create dangerous traps and ambushes.
Be Creative: make it *look* like a wrecked ship or a lava-world.
Name: pick a unique descriptive name for your level.
Separate: each type of level is saved in its own folder.
Overwrite: choosing an existing name will save over that file.
Submit: upload your creations to the AI DB. They may be included in the game!
Best: send your best work, but don't be afraid to participate ;)
Don't: don't add a file extension or use any special characters like /*!% etc.
Approaching Infinity will adapt your creation to its own needs.
Terrain *images* (trees, walls, etc.) will change depending on
the planet type and other procedural factors.
Boss monsters will be created as necessary.
Sometimes it will even re-populate your level with items and monsters.
These features keep it fresh even after multiple plays.
Steam: you must be logged in to Steam to use the level editor.
Sector: you must reach sector 5 in the game before you can make levels.
Time: you may only submit (upload) one level every 2 minutes,
so if you plan to make several, make one, upload it, and make the next.
Items: only certain creatures and items are available for a given level type.

1,Piercing,/A large amount of force concentrated in a small area, to penetrate. The default damage type of solid-projectile weapons, as well as knives./
2,Cutting,/Sharpness applied over a large area, to slice open. The default damage type of swords, and also the damage type caused by monofilament weapons./
3,Smashing,/Excessive force applied with a blunt surface, to crush. The default damage type of hammers, as well as concussion-type guns./
4,Hybrid,/Several different types of physical damage and directions of force, applied simultaneously. A rare damage type that is difficult to defend against./
5,Incendiary,/Whether it's a bullet filled with a flammable compound, a super-hot beam of energy, or an actual burst of flames, incendiary damage lights things on fire./
6,Cryo,/Get supercool, superfast. Cryo damage freezes things. They may become immobilized or brittle. Liquids may freeze solid./
7,Explosive,/Bullets, grenades, and rockets can explode. Beams can't. Explosive damage is forceful, widespread, and difficult to defend against./
8,Corrosive,/Corrosive weapons deliver a strong universal mix of acids. Metal is especially susceptible. Projectiles can be modified to deal corrosive damage, or acid may be sprayed directly./
9,Shock,/Weaponized electricity, usually delivered via capacitor bullets, but can also be fired directly by lightning weapons. Charge can travel through metal and water./
10,Sonic,/Powerful focused sound-waves in a tight beam. Requires an atmospheric pressure between .5 and 2.5 to function. Sonic weapons are often light-weight and rapid-firing./

11,Scrambler,/An 'electronic warfare' effect, meant to disrupt the functioning of electrical systems. Most useful against artificial and silicon-based life. Has little effect on other types of creatures./
12,Xenocide,/A cloud of gas that will quickly destroy plant-life and is also deadly to most insects./
13,Disruptor,/An energy-weapon effect that reduces molecular cohesion. Difficult to defend against. Targets will slowly disintegrate, taking damage over time./
14,Neutron,/A focused beam of neutral particles with great range and penetration, causing direct internal damage to most living things. Hits everything on the way to the target./

15,Fear,/This energy effect disrupts a creature's nervous system directly, often causing them to flee in terror. Causes very little actual damage, and has no effect on artificial or sessile lifeforms./
16,Stun,/Whether by excessive light and sound, concussive force, or direct energy manipulation, stun damage seeks to temporarily immobilize a target./
17,Toxic,/Either a cloud of poisonous gas or bullets laced with near-universal fast-acting toxins. Has little effect on non-living creatures./
18,Ion,/A burst of charged particles that shocks and disrupts electrical systems, including that of living things. Can't be delivered by standard slug-throwers./
19,Plasma,/A concentrated burst of charged superheated matter, doing both burning and electrical damage simultaneously. Has great penetration. Found almost exclusively in energy weapons./
20,Graviton,/Weaponized gravity waves rend and thrust the target. Very hard to defend against./
21,Nano,/A dangerous weapon that releases a swarm of hungry nano-bots upon impact. These quickly disassemble their target, but may also spread and destroy natural planetary features./
22,Nuclear,/One of the most powerful and dangerous types of energy, harnessed for use as a weapon./
23,Tangler,/A sticky polymer expands rapidly then hardens, trapping the target./
24,Grappler,/A mechanical contraption that latches onto a creature and pulls it closer. Only available on ballistic weapons like pistols and rifles. Disables "Return Fire" ability of rifles./
25,Cage,/A self-assembling prison cell with room for one. Grenade only.
32,Extraction,/A powerful combination of forces and energies designed to render a creature down to its constituent elements./

The glyphs are etched into my mind, and I can perceive little else, whether in my thoughts or right in front of me... my clarity is fading... my final thoughts are of sector 50, though I've never been there.

I was right, this world was once inhabited by the Protomonoco, their relics are everywhere! The place is strangely quiet too, but that's even better for our work. Wait, what was that? Look out! @anyoldmonster!

I've confirmed it, this is another former Protomonoco colony. @civilianname_ra has uncovered several cultural relics that are close matches to their style. Unfortunately, they've also come down with a case of @localdisease... I'm sure it will pass.

@racecaptain_ra sent me to lead the search for the stolen @nameoftheitem. What were they doing before I got here? It's right over there! I'm going to send @individualname_ra to go get it. Should I mention all those @lotsofmonsters...

I think the entire landing party is having a bad reaction to the @rareplantname in the area. It's the only thing we haven't accounted for. Imagine me, @individualname_ra, laid to rest by a plant. And it's not even trying to eat us or burn us or shooting poison darts... a plant...
I'll admit it, we're lost. Exhausted and lost. @individualname_ra is already unconscious. I know there's a @themonsterinstance prowling around, but I think we're done for, one way or another.

@individualname_ra's personal journal: We are the last surviving crew members from @randomshipname. A @randomotherrace squadron attacked us. We still don't know why, but it hardly matters now. No one is coming to save us. I don't know if anyone will even find this recording. If you do, remember us.
It seems like we've been wandering for days, this planet is huge! Everyone else has given up and now it's my turn to lead... I think the shuttle is this way?
This has been fun, I forgot what this ephemeral existence was like. All that's left to do now is 'die'.
@individualname_ra went crazy after carring the @nameofthedevice for too long... ran off with it and is now picking us off one by one, from some hiding place.
The ship's readings must have been off, or else winter's coming fast. It just keeps getting colder.
Our bodies aren't built to handle these temperatures, and our tech can't keep up. Ice is forming over @individualname_ra's body already.
Whatever poisons are in the air here, our suits can't keep them out.
@individualname_ra's log: Despite the near-perfect nitrogen/oxygen mix, I think the @tracegas is having an unexpected effect on us. @racecaptain_ra doesn't believe me.
We've all been bitten or stung by some kind of insect multiple times. @individualname_ra's bites are swelling, and I think I saw movement under the skin...

We're all done for, we can't escape that @anyoldmonster, and this world will be our final resting place. I wonder what the local decay processes are like? Maybe I should have been a biologist? Too late now.
We weren't prepared for this. Some of our equipment is eroding as I watch, decaying like rotten fruit. I don't think they'll attempt a rescue. @individualname_ra chose to get it over with quickly.

Nothing can prepare you for this kind of heat. I watched, nearly paralyzed, as @individualname_ra practically melted away next to some lava. We're prepping the transport for return but I think it will be too late.
I'm pinned to the surface by my own weight, can barely move, and I'm not getting any response from @individualname_ra. How does any living thing survive this?

The ambient radiation is far beyond anything the landing party is equipped for. For me, it started with my vision. Others lost motor control. Even if we get off this world, I don't think we'll survive.

This planet never stops shaking! We've lost our way because the terrain keeps changing, boulders poke up from underground, sometimes waiting for the slightest disturbance to collapse. What did @racecaptain_ra hope to find?
We had hoped to discover what processes this planet is undergoing to cause it to be so dangerous. So far, we have only learned how fragile our lives are. I will remember you, @individualname_ra.
I can't believe @individualname_ra put the @nameoftheitem down and doesn't remember where. @racecaptain_ra won't let us back on the ship without it! We won't last forever down here.

We got a tip that there's a @nameofthedevice just lying around somewhere down here, but we haven't found it yet. And with that @anyoldmonster, we're not exactly free to move around. We're going to make a move soon.
These caverns seem to loop back on themselves, while only ever leading further away from the exit. None of us has any idea which way to go.
Our expedition takes us further underground. Unfortunately, we have discovered a @themonsterinstance. Or maybe it discovered us?
I am beginning to think these caves might go on forever. Our progress, however, may be cut short by the @hazardname.
I don't understand what organics find so relaxing about island planets.
@racecaptain_ra finally granted our request for leave on an island planet. The crew is ready to relax. But I've got a bad feeling about this place... I think I smell @whatevertheproblemis.

@individualname_ra reporting from the science team sent to investigate what happened to the colony on @nameofthisplanet. Preliminary findings suggest a major environmental shift, but it may also have had something to do with the @whatevertheproblemis.
We're beginning our survey and we've just detected @whatevertheproblemis. Either the ship's scanners are malfunctioning, or the captain didn't want us to worry. Or maybe just wanted us dead?

What kind of value could such an uninviting world have? Surveying this planet will be a nightmare! Even if we succeed, who would be willing to pay for this? @racecaptain_ra, can we return to the ship?
This planet is teeming with life, and rather beautiful. Except for the swarming insects. If this unit had 'skin', those would be intolerable.
Trees. That's what we found. Trees and more trees. Can't even see the jungle. Just trees. Next time we need to bring down some cutting equipment. Oh wait, there's a-- No another tree.

We have come here to @nameofthisplanet to study the so-called "kelp-horse", and attempt to discover by what means it fertilizes, stimulates, or otherwise positively interacts with its environment. So far, we have learned very little, but our mission has just begun.
These kelp-horses seem to make plants grow. If we could transport them off-world, we could improve our colony's agricultural output. We'll just need to steer clear of the @whatevertheproblemis.
An animal that grows plants? There's gotta be a way to profit from that. Hey @civilianname_ra! Stop taunting that @themonsterinstance and help em round up these kelp-horses.

I'm sending @individualname_ra to investigate a strange structure we found. Can't tell from here whether it's organic or some kind of exotic mineral. It looks like it might have something inside it. Wait. It's opening...
I never understood what beauty was before. @civilianname_ra, are you seeing this? I'm going to sit down for a while and appreciate this.
This world would be a death sentence for a less mentally evolved species. Luckily, hypno-flowers have no power over us. All we have to worry about is the @whatevertheproblemis.
We wish to examine those flowers more closely. They are emitting unique radiation. Unfortunately this @themonsterinstance is in the way.
We're really taking a beating from this '@bossmonstername'. Concentrate your fire on the--

We're done for. Radiation scrambled our insides. There was some kind of creature in there, writhing in the middle of it all, like it was feeding off the emissions. It kept pulling us in, dragging us into the hot zone. We managed to escape, but like I said, we're done for.
What is it? Get it off me! Ouch, hey! It bit me. Ugh, I don't feel so good. Everything's going dark... Hey, @civilianname_ra, are you still there? Oh, there's another one on me. Help!
Yenog has glow cubes? Yenog has glow cubes! @individualname_ra will take glow cubes. Attack!
If we're gonna be down here, and we gotta fight for our lives, we might as well smash that yenog and grab all the gemstones that fall out of it!

All attempts to initiate intelligent discourse with the silicoid life-form known as a "yenog" have failed. Several members of my team have fallen from its attacks. I must reconsider my priorities, and pass on this knowledge so that no future attempts at communication are made.
That yenog's got us pinned down. I'm going to send @individualname_ra to draw its attention while I move in for a power-strike with my hammer. Get ready!
What's with these purple eggs? They're pulsing like they might burst. @individualname_ra, you take point. We're going to take a closer look.

We continue to document the spread of the squither life-form across local space. The scope of this tragedy is immense, something must be done. Wait. @individualname_ra follow protocols! You are too close, move away now.
We've found another one. These bugs are building hives in our territory. This is starting to look like more than just a random occurrence. We need more intel. Wait... I see one now: a Narcratu!
Looks like we stumbled into one of those Narcratu hives. @individualname_ra stopped us just in time. We're gonna back out nice and slow.

Narcratu communication attempt #3, this time within what appears to be some sort of underground hive. So far, all encounters have ended in tactical withdrawal. Perhaps we can learn something from this environment?

We've come across some sort of underground forest. Golden pollen drifts through the air, sometimes gathering and solidifying deposits, possibly on some sticky substance? I've never seen plant-life like this before, and I believe I hear faint music... what is happening here?

@individualname_ra leading the search and salvage team on @nameofthisplanet. It's going to be tough, there are a lot of @lotsofmonsters among the wreckage. I'm not sure if this one's worth it, but we're going to make a preliminary sweep.
No survivors here, that ship really came apart. We'll take a look around, but all we've seen so far is a @themonsterinstance. Might be something worth salvaging...

:D E S C:::More data from pickups
2 ` this starts at 2 because its a multiplier and 5x1=5 (no increase)
Increases the amount of data you get from anything that is actively picked up, like spatial anomalies or datapads, by +100% per level. Does not increase general exploration data.
:D E S C:::More data from exploration
Gather more data from exploration in all locations: +100% per level.
:D E S C:::Helps to identify artifacts
Helps to identify artifacts by eliminating some of the wrong choices automatically. Also, sometimes a clue you find will count as two.
:D E S C:::Prevent or cure disease

Reduces the chances of contracting diseases, and constantly works to cure them. Level 2 will suggest a method of curing disease with rare plants. Level 3 offers another option. [Level] is halved when dealing with mutated diseases.
:D E S C:::Some creatures won't attack.

Some creatures become non-hostile. If you move into their space, you examine them for DNA (25%/level) and essences (10%/level). Level 1: plants and prey animals. Level 2: insect, aquatic, and silicon life-forms. Level 3: predators, slimes, and apex creatures.
:D E S C:::Constantly heals away team

Provides a small but constant healing effect to the away team, and speeds natural recovery when resting. Also speeds recovery of injured officers. Level 2 allows officers who are injured more than 100 to heal while on away missions.
Reduces the damage and duration of status effects like fire and poison, and gives +5 (or +5%) environmental resistance per point.
:D E S C:::Damage bonus on away missions
Attack the target's soft spots to deal +20% damage per level of this skill.
Squeeze a little extra speed out of your engines (+15 per level). High speed allows you to move more often than your enemies.
:D E S C:::Slowly repairs hull damage
Slowly repairs your ship's hull over time, by about 1% per level every 3 turns. Also speeds up shuttle repair.
:D E S C:::Increase maximum shield strength
Increases the maximum strength of your shields by 20% per level, allowing them to repel more damage.

Allows asteroid mining. At level 1, items spawned from asteroid mining are automatically collected. Level 2 automatically mines adjacent asteroids. Higher levels increase auto-mining distance. Every 2 levels increases the amount of Ice-23 mined.
:D E S C:::Require fewer essences to craft
Decreases the number of each type of Essences that is required to craft an item by [level]. It can never be less than 1.
:D E S C:::Craft much better components
Your engineering knowledge increases the quality of components you craft by 10% per level.
:D E S C:::Reduce cooldowns on secondary systems
Speeds up the cooldown process of any system with a long cooldown (>12 turns), even some weapons. Level 2 reduces the threshold to 10 turns, and can reduce very long cooldowns by 4 every turn!
:D E S C:::Oxygen supply lasts longer
Gives a 20% chance per level that each turn on an away mission will not consume oxygen. Chance caps at 90%.
:D E S C:::Increases away team hp.
Increases the away team's hp by +20% per level.
:D E S C:::Increase planet movement speed
Increases the movement speed of the away team by +15 per level, allowing you to out-maneuver your enemies.
:D E S C:::Innate knowledge of caves

Reveals cave entrances and stairs. Find more oxy-algae. Level 2 allows digging dirt and rubble, and scans will always detect caves. Level 3 shows the depth of caves in scans and reveals hidden underground areas. Each level increases quality of items mined from rich dirt.
:D E S C:::Away team gets better cover bonus
For each level, take 10% less damage in any terrain that provides cover (blocks sight), and do 10% more damage.
:D E S C:::More data from alien life
Extra data (+2 per level) on away missions from kills and passively analyzing large plant-life. Also allows automatic, one-time analysis of certain plant-life for +100 data per skill level.
:D E S C:::Data and resource bonus
Increases data (+1 per level) from mountains and caves revealed. Also increases planetary resources found, and amount of metallicum mined.
:D E S C:::Reveal terrain, easier surveys
Reveal planetary terrain features when landing, like mountains, water, or trees. Higher levels reveal more features. Also allows planetary surveys to be completed at less than 100% (-5% per level.)
Level 1 fixes damaged floors for free. Level 2 gives 'magnetic boots' power. Level 3 removes damaged walls.
:D E S C:::Increased ship weapon damage
This skill increases the damage of all your ship weapons by 15% per level.
:D E S C:::Reduce Weapon Cooldown And Supply Use
Decreases the supply usage (50% at level 1, 66% at level 2) of all ship weapons and reduces the cooldowns on slow firing (>5 turns) weapons by 1 per level.
:D E S C:::Increase shield recharge, reduce cooldown
Increases the recharge amount on your shields by 33% per level, and also reduces their cooldown time.
:D E S C:::Increase away team hp and damage
Increases the away team's hit points and damage inflicted by 15%.
With precise aim (and this skill), the away team's effective firing range is increased by 1 per level.
:D E S C:::Bonus damage to non-hostile creatures
Do an extra 50% damage per level to entities not already attacking you.
:D E S C:::Do more melee damage
Each level of this skill gives a 50% damage bonus to all melee attacks.
The away team will automatically strike back at any creature that melee attacks them. Each level grants 1 strike-back per turn.
:D E S C:::More scanning details and higher decloak radius.
Automatically decipher more information about scanned planets and shipwrecks (+3 per level). Also increases the distance you can detect cloaked ships by 1 per level.
Increases sensor range (+1 per level), which speeds up exploration and gives earlier threat detection.
:D E S C:::Reduces damage to your ship
Reduces damage to your ship from most sources, including space hazards, cannon and missile weapons (but not beams), by 15% per level.
:D E S C:::Harder for enemies to find you
Reduces the distance at which enemy ships may become hostile, by 1 tile per level. Also reduces the distance at which enemy ships can break your cloak, by 1 tile per level (can reduce it to 0).
Reduces the overall supply usage of your ship by 3 per turn per level. Also reduces away mission supply cost by 10% per level (max 75%, officer does not need to join away team).
:D E S C:::Reveal large objects in new sectors
Allows you to infer the existence of large objects within a sector. Level 2 also reveals artificial objects. Level 3 reveals entities every 25 turns!
:D E S C:::Know the outline of shipwrecks in advance
Level 1 reveals the outer border of all shipwrecks you dock with. Level 2 shows all bulkheads. Level 3 reveals vital machines like life support and command consoles.
Choose your landing spot on planetary missions. Increases away mission supply cost by 50. Higher levels allow more precise landings in tighter spaces. Officer must accompany away team.
:D E S C:::Hire more crew at less cost
Reduces the cost of hiring crew. Each level increases maximum crew size by 5 and maximum away team size by 1.
:D E S C:::Better relations with aliens
Increases the rate at which you earn positive reputation with all alien species, by +100% per level.
:D E S C:::Store more cargo in less space
This skill increases the amount of cargo your ship's hold can carry, by +5 per level.
Increases your base supply storage capacity by +1000 per level. Great for long trips.
:D E S C:::Increase pawn shop selling prices
Increases the amount of credits you get for all items sold in space station pawn shops by 25% per level. Also increases how much you get for selling surveys and towed shipwrecks.
Increase the chance that aliens will come to your aid (or show leniency) when hailed, by about 20% per level. They might also talk more often.
:D E S C:::Help officers gain experience
All officers will receive bonus XP (+1 per level) for anything that already grants more than 1xp.
:D E S C:::Enemy ships may drop items when shot
Gives a 20% chance per level that enemy ships will drop something of value every time you shoot them.
:D E S C:::Dock at any station

If your reputation with a faction is too low, you have the opportunity to pay a bribe to dock at their stations. Higher levels reduce the bribe cost and remove rep-based price penalities in the station. Level 3 allows you to complete quests for any faction.
:D E S C:::Longer cloak duration, faster cooldown
Reduces the cooldown of all cloaking devices by about -10% per level. Tactical cloaks last longer (+2 turns per level).
:D E S C:::Create more intact shipwrecks
Increases the chance of a shipwreck being created when an enemy ship is destroyed by 25% per level.
Interferes with enemy ships calling for help (25% chance per level). Decreases reputation loss. Gives a small chance (12% per level) that ships won't realize it was you that shot them.
:D E S C:::Increase away team sight range
Increases the away team's sight range by +1 per level.
:D E S C:::Pickups heal away team
Picking up items heals the away team by about 10% per level. Also halves the cooldown on the natural healing timer.
:D E S C:::Less chance of activating traps
On away missions, reduces the chance of triggering proximity traps like cave-ins and short circuits by 30% per level. Max 95%.
:D E S C:::Reduces detection of away team
Reduces the distance at which monsters may become hostile, by one tile per level.
Detect basic quest items at a distance. Level 2 reveals Firax objects, and level 3 finds almost all quest items.
:D E S C:::Away team can cross water
Away team can cross water. Level 2 eliminates the movement speed penalty. Level 3 gives +50 speed on water!
:D E S C:::Away team can cross mountains
Away team can cross mountains. Level 2 eliminates the movement speed penalty and reduces damage from earthquakes and cave-in traps.
:D E S C:::Away team can cross acid
Away team can cross acid lakes and rivers. Level 2 eliminates the movement speed penalty, and reduces the duration of 'poison' status effects.
:D E S C:::Away team can cross lava
Away team can cross cross lava. Level 2 eliminates the movement speed penalty, and reduces the duration of 'burn' status effects.
:D E S C:::Away team can dissipate forcefields
Away team bumps to dissipate force-fields. Each level of the skill eliminates one color of field: red, blue, yellow, purple.
:D E S C:::Defense against laser gates and radiation.
Away team takes less damage from laser-gates and irradiated tiles. Does not affect landing on irradiated planets. Higher levels give more protection. Prevents officer injuries due to laser gates.
:D E S C:::Away team can bump to remove rubble
Away team can bump to remove rubble. Can dig through cave walls at level 2. Higher levels make digging easier and faster.
:D E S C:::Warp further, more often.
Your warp drive recharges faster and can jump further (+1 sector per level). At level 3 you can use wormholes as warp points!
:D E S C:::Protects ship from space hazards
Take no damage from radiation belts at level 1, ion storms at level 2, and black holes at level 3.
:D E S C:::Chance to disarm space-mines
Detect space-mines at greater distance, and get 35% chance per level to disarm them when moving into minefields.
:D E S C:::Absorb nebula for supplies
Absorb nebula to create supplies (+100 per level). Level 2 gives more supplies and level 3 works on dark nebula too.
Allows asteroid mining. Travel through and disperse dense asteroid fields. Higher levels increase the chance of finding mineable asteroids. Every 2 levels increases the amount of Ice-23 mined.
:D E S C:::Increase chance of weapon effects
Increases the chances that weapons with powers like cryo and incendiary will activate their special effects, by 33% per level. Increases the effectiveness of stun and tangler weapons.
The away team automatically cuts down nearby large plant-life and harms plant-monsters. Higher levels yields larger radius. Level 2 instantly destroys webs on the away team.
:D E S C:::Collect blood for data
Collect blood samples to gain data. Level 2 gives an oxygen boost, and level 3 provides minor healing. Each level gives an increased chance that you can harvest DNA from blood.
:D E S C:::Mercs won't attack you

Mercenaries won't attack you in most situations (unless you're on a mission for their enemies). +20 rep with Mercenaries per level. Find underground Merc bases at depth equal to [Level]. Level 1 granted 'naturally' with 150 infamy.
:D E S C:::Escape pursuers in nebula
Flying through nebula, radiation belts, or ion storms has a 12% chance per level per turn to make one of your pursuers stop looking for you.
:D E S C:::Ship weapons fire farther
Increases the firing range of all ship weapons, by +1 per level.
:D E S C:::Increase away team weapon spread
Increases the number of adjacent targets hit with weapons that hit more than one target.
:D E S C:::More damage vs. Bosses
Increases damage to all "boss" creatures and ships by 25% per level.
Throw grenades one additional tile per level.
:D E S C:::Fight harder when dying
When the away team is badly injured they become inspired and receive a bonus to movement speed (+20 per level) and melee damage (+50% per level).
:D E S C:::Lockers spawn more loot
Increases the frequency and amount of many kinds of loot drops, and value of credit pickups. Also increases chance of finding items in lockers and other containers by about 10% per level.
:D E S C:::Creates credits every turn
Automatically adds [level x 100] credits per turn from an unknown source...
:D E S C:::Hide illegal cargo from scans
Hides up to 15 cargo units per level of contraband goods and illegal weapons from scanners. Gives 10% bonus per skill level to credits received from smuggling.
:D E S C:::Hailed ships may pay you and run

When hailing ships, there is a 20% chance per level that they will drop valuables and head for the warp point. Get -1 rep with that faction and +5 infamy per success. Doesn't work on Gruff, Bankers, Firax, or Eaters.
:D E S C:::Pay less for everything
Pay 5% less per level for everything. This is not reflected in prices, and there is no record of it. You underpay everyone, and you get away with it.
:D E S C:::Pick up nearby items
At level 1, on away missions pick up items within radius 1. level 2: space radius 1. level 3: away team, radius 2. Level 4: space, radius 2. No further benefit of higher levels.
:D E S C:::Do more toxic damage
On away missions, your toxic weapons deal 100% more damage per level. In space, when using the toxic penetrator weapon, kills one additional crew per level.
:D E S C:::Increases cannon weapon damage
Increases the damage of your ship's cannon weapons by 50% per level.
:D E S C:::Better armor, take fewer crits
Hits to your armor (not shields) do 15% less damage per level, and there is a 15% chance per level to negate any critical hits received.
:D E S C:::Deal more critical hits
Get +15% per level that your attacks (both in space and away missions) will inflict critical hits.
:D E S C:::Melee attacks hit more targets
Your melee attacks hit an additional [level] hostile targets, either adjacent to you or your target.
:D E S C:::Deal devastating damage, get grenades.

There is a 20% chance per level that the away team's guns (pistol, rifle, shotgun, smg, sniper) will deal damage that the target is weak against. Also grants a 1% chance per turn per level to restore depleted grenade ammo.

Use your melee attack to tame up to [level] creatures (predator, apex, insect, silicon only) to become your allies on this map. Level 1 butchers prey animals into food, and level 2 catches aquatic creatures. Level 3 begrudgingly makes plant monsters into food.
:D E S C:::Reduce heavy weapon penalties

Removes some penalties from away team heavy weapons. At level 1, -1 sniper range penalty. Level 2: -1 launcher cooldown. Level 3: -1 cloudgun and grappler cooldown. Level 4: an additional -1 launcher cooldown.
:D E S C:::Get paid for killing pirate ships
Instantly receive $5,000 per level for every pirate, merc, or syndicate ship destroyed.
Get paid 33% more per level for all quests upon completion.
:D E S C:::Become cloaked in nebula
As long as you're not in red alert, your ship becomes cloaked while in sight-blocking terrain at level 1, and asteroids and shipwrecks at level 2.
:D E S C:::Capture criminals for cash

Automatically capture certain enemies within a [level]-tile radius: pirates (level 1), mercs (level 2), syndicate members (level 3). Take captured criminals to Limoquee or Banker stations for bounty payment.
Automatically dodge [level] attacks per turn while standing in doorways. At level 2, it works for anything that gives the away team 50% cover, and at level 3, the threshold is 35% cover.
:D E S C:::Augments supplies and cargo
Reveals stations and warp points. Use [level x 2] fewer supplies per turn. Carry [level x 5] more cargo and [level x 750] more supplies.
:D E S C:::Buy lower, sell higher
Reduces the cost of buying commodities, and increases the price you sell them for. At level 3, get real-time price data in all sectors.
:D E S C:::Commodities take up less space
Carry 25% more commodities per cargo space per level, always at least +1. (For example, 25 food instead of 20, or 2 antimatter instead of 1.)
:D E S C:::Harvest more rare plants
Get a 25% chance per level to harvest one additional sample of a rare plant, and 25% per level to leave behind "something growing" when harvesting (max 90%), which can be fertilized to grow again.
:D E S C:::Go where you want to go
At level 1, the away team is immune to webs and slime. At level 2, they can't be pushed or pulled. At level 3, your ship can not be pushed or pulled.
:D E S C:::Move to melee attack distant enemies

On away missions, when moving towards an enemy, if moving an additional [level] tiles in a straight line would put you next to that enemy, then move the entire distance and melee attack it. Does not activate if you are already next to an enemy.

Sally Cormick Races the Devil, Part 1 : Goggles on. Engines hot. There's an old saying, you can't outrace the devil. Sally 'Blaze' Cormick looked over at the glowing red ship resting next to her at the starting line. Five. The count down started. Four. Gloved hands flexed. Three. They closed around the star racer's yolk. Two. A deep breath, fingers gripping so tight they go numb. One. The moment before the start stretched out into infinity like light tumbling down a black hole.

Sally Cormick Races the Devil, Part 2 :  She'd won. She'd won everything. The interstellar Tracks. The Light Speed Prix. Even the illegal circuits, like Meteor Blitz and Galaxy's End. Life was victory and speed, and what else was there? No one could catch her. And then, they stopped trying. They weren’t even races anymore. Not for her, they jockeyed for second or third, and she... she retired. She tried other things, but it was all so bland and slow. So she was just boredly looking out at the heavy turtle's march to death, that is, until he came by.

Sally Cormick Races the Devil, Part 3 :  A glowing red ship. It seemed to move a thousand miles an hour even sitting still. She didn't listen to what he had to say, his hat in his hand. A race? Her soul? Eternal damnation? All she could feel was that thrill, like the first time all over again. It was on the starting line that she stopped long enough to consider, in that moment between the countdown and the engine flare. Beat the devil. Couldn't be done. All she could do was grin.

Sally Cormick Races the Devil, Part 4 :  GO! The universe blurred. At speeds where flight was instinct. Where thought made you slow. Got you killed. She was back. And maybe for the first time, someone was right there with her. That glowing red ship, had given her a lead. Her! Ha! But now, it gained. It gained fast. She hit the bend at the quasar perfectly, and the red ship gained. She clocked in her fastest time, THE fastest time on the titan belt, and the red ship gained. The final stretch, just empty space and the goal. The red ship gained. Her grin widened.

Sally Cormick Races the Devil, Part 5 :  Her dashboard was nothing but lights. Flashing, warning. The red ship gained. Soon, her dash was nothing but red. Her star racer buckled. She felt it give. Parts of it tearoff. And the red ship was neck and neck. Her grin widened still, as the explosion engulfed her ship. Nothing but flame crossed the finish line. Twisted gnarled bits of gleaming metal, still orange with heat. The red ship floated over to the wreckage.

Sally Cormick Races the Devil, Part 6 :  A hospital bed. An IV. A broken body now held together by bolts and bandages. Dour faced doctors with dour prognoses. The headlines loved it, Famous Star Racer! Sally'Blaze' Cormick, Critical condition! They came to visit. Flowers. Presents. She didn't even look up. Not until he came. You won. He admitted, hat in hand. What do you want? Her good eye, the other a mess of gauze, rolled over to look at him. Again. She said. Let's race again. All he could do was grin.

The universe is made up of maps. Most terrains are passable, but some (like walls and dense asteroid belts) are not. Some terrain can be modified or destroyed.``Map tiles are unknown until you've seen them, so exploration is key to finding what you need.``If you don't know what something is, put the cursor over it and hold [SHIFT] to tooltip.`There are tooltip settings near the top of the options menu.``Space is divided into "sectors" which contain stars, planets, asteroids, shipwrecks, space stations, nebula, ships, and basically everything. There are an infinite number of sectors...``A sector is *not* a star system, and one tile on the map does not indicate any specific unit of distance. Scale is abstract!``You can send your away team for missions on planets, shipwrecks, star temples and more. The map is usually centered around you (either your ship or away team).`You can zoom in or out with the mouse scroll wheel or [control+plus] and [control+minus].`(This and other hotkey combos are detailed in Options => Keybinds.)``If you zoom out far enough, the map snaps to a central static location, and you can see the whole thing at once. Away team may begin to heal.`&78 Safety [S] &99 : Toggle your weapon's safety setting. When safety is on, you will not fire at non-hostile (or potentially non-hostile) targets.`&78 Make Note [N] &99 : Leave yourself a note on the map: an officer you want to hire, a planet you couldn't complete, a dangerous enemy, etc.`&78 Use [U] &99 : Use a consumable. Use gel to speed up skill cooldowns, fix your armor with hull paste, or throw down an auto-turret.`&78 Build/Repair [B] &99 : On away missions, you can build walls, fix floors, and repair machinery. Often requires scrap metal or crafting parts. Can also be used to place a Porta-Door.``You can see the entire command list in Options => Keybinds. This can be helpful even if you play with the mouse. There might be some things you didn't know were possible.

"Cooldown" refers to a period of time (in turns) before an items or power can be used again.``Weapons, warp drive, and activated skills all have cooldowns.``Learning to manage your cooldowns in difficult situations is essential.``There are some skills that lower the cooldowns of specific types of items. Cyber-skill cooldowns can be reduced by using gel. "Coolant cream" can be applied to ship components.``Skill cooldowns are shown as numbers on their icons. Component cooldowns are shown as status icons (or text) on the middle right of the hud.``You can even see the cooldowns on an enemy ship's weapons by looking at their tooltip.

Whether you call them entities, creatures, mobs, or monsters, there are other *things* in the universe that move and shoot too. Sometimes they move *towards* you, and shoot *at* you. Look out!``Most spaceships are going somewhere: patroling, searching for loot, or heading to a station. `Creatures on away missions may be lying in wait, wandering aimlessly, or actively hunting.``Some beings are natural enemies of other beings. Predators eat prey. Pirates attack Sigorn. Gruff want to fight almost anything. ``Entities have a lot of the same things you have: hull and shields or HP. Weapons or other means to do damage.``Some have additional powers, whether like yours or feats beyond your capabilities.`Sometimes they have friends too, and attacking one means more will show up.``Many creatures encountered on away missions have local adaptations: extra powers that their kind doesn't usually possess, making them more dangerous and unpredictable.`These will be indicated in their name, and briefly explained in their tooltip.``Remember you can hail spaceships to talk to them. This is a great way to learn about them, make new friends, or even save someone's life by initiating surrender.``Ships may hail you from time to time, whether to talk, threaten, or even ask for help.

Loot refers to just about anything that can be picked up and has some value.`When you move into a tile, you automatically pick up any loot there.``• &78 Components&99 : weapons, defenses, engines, suits, and devices. Items you can use to upgrade your loadout. Every component or device takes up 1 cargo space.`• &78 Commodities&99 : the 13 common trade-goods from boxes to antimatter.`Most commodities take up a fraction of 1 cargo unit.`Note: "food" is a trade-good and is *not* required for your crew to eat.``All other types of loot don't take up cargo space&99 :``• &78 Quest items&99 : flowers, minerals, books, clues. Anything that anyone could want.`• &78 Crafting parts&99 : all major components can be built using the 14 crafting parts. `• &78 Consumables&99 : single-use items that provide a variety of useful effects.`• &78 Gadgets&99 : esoteric contraptions used in the repair of vital ship systems.`• &78 Plants and essences&99 : samples of rare plants and vital essences, often used in crafting and modding items.`• &78 Datapads&99 : Captains are always leaving log reports laying around...`• &78 DNA&99 : scanning a creature's genetic information will help you understand it (and kill it).`• &78 Credits&99 : pure galactic currency waiting to be picked up.`• &78 Traps&99 : Not loot, but if you walk into acid, biohazards, radiation, or fire, you'll be exposed.`• &78 The Amulet of Yendor&99 : It's probably just a cheap plastic copy...`• &78 AND SO MUCH MORE!&99 : there are so many things you can find. Remember you can tooltip items for a quick description, or check your message log to see what you picked up.

Time is an abstract concept. Time passes when you end your turn (either by moving or waiting, or on away missions only, by attacking).``Let me say that again: In space, you can shoot and then move, all on the same turn.`But on away missions, moving *or* attacking will end your turn.``Another measure of time is Star Date, which is always displayed at the top left. `You are invited to speculate about what each group of numbers means.`Star Date goes up every turn, more in space than on away missions.``You can see how many turns you've played in Infinipedia => Stats, under "accomplishments".``Some rare occurrences can cause you to lose one or more turns, such as time dilation near black holes, or gazing at the beauty of the hypno-flower.

Speed is "how long it takes you to complete an action, relative to the entities around you", `so it relates in some ways to time and turns.``The average speed is 200. A speed of 350 is almost twice as fast, and 50 would be 4 times slower! All entities (ships, creatures) have their own speed stat which you can see in their tooltip.``If you notice an entity moving or attacking multiple times after your turn, they are probably much faster than you.``Your ship's speed is calculated from its base speed (determined by ship class), armor, engines, reactor, and any relevant skills, devices, or powers.``Away team speed is based on your suit, main, swap, and melee weapons, as well as skills, devices, and powers. Away team speed can also be affected by terrain and gravity.``Speed Ratio:``On an entity's tooltip, you may notice after their speed stat, a ratio like (4:5).``This means that it will move 4 times for every 5 moves you get (in this case, it's a little slower than you). If the ratio is 2:1, look out! It will move twice as fast (often) as you! ``Speed is one of the hardest concepts for some people to grasp in Approaching Infinity. Sorry.`If nothing else, know that having a high speed is good.

Space stations are great centers of galactic commerce. Buy supplies, hire crew, trade components and commodities, receive quests, even buy a new ship. It would be hard to get anything done without space stations. Bankers stations are in almost every sector, and there is usually one embassy of another major faction present.``When your crew is infected with a disease, a space station is your best hope for a cure, although not all species are equipped (or inclined) to treat human illnesses.  Stations are also the place where most quests get completed or "turned in".`&78 `Lobby &99 : You start at the entrance of the lobby, where you get a rundown of the faction in charge, including your reputation and their relative power in the galaxy. This is the place to hire crew and officers, buy crafting supplies, sell data, and get quests.`&78 `Market &99 : Here you can buy and sell the 13 major galactic commodities. For many players, these are just "loot", and there is a convenient "Sell Everything" button at the bottom. But for traders, this is where your money is made: buy low here, sell high elsewhere.`&78 `Outfitter &99 : Most stations sell one of just about every kind of component (ship weapons, shields, away team suits and guns, etc.), but faction influences what is actually sold. Scroll down, over 20 items can be found here.`&78 `Pawn Shop &99 : This is where you can sell off your extra gear, as well as surveys and artifacts. Each faction values particular types of surveys.`&78 `Shipyard &99 : Each station sells one type of ship. Faction stations always sell their own ship type, but Bankers stations can sell any one of 8 kinds. When buying a new ship, all your components and cargo transfer, but your ship will then have the appearance, base stats, and built-in devices of the new type.

Crew are humans whose names you rarely learn until they screw up. They are squishy and not very bright. But you need them to help clean the ship and carry stuff on away missions.``Officers are highly trained and trusted individuals. They can lead away missions if the captain can't be bothered. Technically *you* (the captain) are an officer.``Officers get passive skills when they level up, and can use activated cyber-skills.`Crew get killed.``You can't launch away missions if you don't have enough crew.`Away team size is crew divided by 4, and usually maxes out at 12, though those numbers can be increased with skills.``The more crew on the away team, the longer they'll survive.`That's because when your HP reaches 0, a crew member dies, and the HP bar is reset.`If you run out of crew, then officers start dying.`The captain dies last, and then it's game over.``Or the captain can usually stay on the ship. It's up to you.``But:``Officers on away missions gain XP and level up a lot faster than those who stay behind...``Each time an officer levels up, they get a new skill level.`An officer can have a maximum of 6 different skills, and almost all skills have multiple levels.`At level 11, officers can advance their skills beyond normal limits.``You can read more about officers in the "skills" tab farther down.

Quests are missions to complete tasks. They provide rewards and a sense of purpose. Each of the 12 major factions has a quest line to follow, and 8 of those lead to unique victories.``Quests can come from many sources: You start with a few quests, and most stations will offer a quest. There are also a lot of quests out there waiting to be found: books, packages, S.O.S. beacons, and NPCs are a few sources.``Most quests require you to travel to a specific planet or sector, while others can be completed anywhere.``Some quests auto-complete when you've met their conditions, others require you to report back to the faction or person you received them from.``Most quests can be abandoned. If you got the quest from a faction embassy, you will lose reputation with them, but they will probably offer the same quest again.``8 of the 12 major factions offer game-ending victories through the quest chains in their embassies. Don't worry, you will get a warning before accepting a quest that ends your game.``*NOTE: Quest targets are often spawned at the time of map creation, but others are spawned a few at a time (especially enemies). If you can't find what you're looking for, keep looking, even if the area is already explored. There are also failsafes designed to spawn quest targets when a map is loaded, so if all else fails, leave and come back.

Your ship is made up of items ("components") like weapons, defenses, and engines. Each one goes into a special slot, and you can view your current loadout on the Inventory screen.``Upgrading the various components of your ship and away team is a necessary part of survival.`Items can be examined, removed, favorited, and installed in the inventory screen.``Every ship has:``&78 • 3 weapon slots`• 1 Energy Field slot `• 1 Armor slot `• 1 Sensor slot`• 1 Engine slot`• 1 Warp Drive slot`• 1 Reactor slot`• 0, 1, or 2 "built-in devices", according to ship class.`• 6 device slots```&99 Your away team gear is also made up of:``&78 • Main Gun slot `• Swap Gun slot `• Melee Weapon slot `• Suit slot`• Grenade slot`• Device slot`

Most items have stats: numbers that tell how good an item is at a particular task, like damaging your enemies or keeping you alive. Here are some examples:`&12 `Heavy Autocannon`DM:82 [41] RN:4 CD:2 PD:4 SU:30``Superior Shield`SHE:780 RCH:120 CD:4 SU:22``Lightning Cloudgun`DM:131 RN:5 ADJ:10 NOK:2 SPD:-30`&99 `The stats of every component are explained in detail in the following topics.``Bigger numbers are usually better, and since the name of the game is "Approaching Infinity", most numbers just keep going up...

&16 Builds are individual layouts for ship components, devices, and away team gear.` &99 `Create builds focused on a particular weapon or pupose like stealth, trade, or survey, and switch between them.``On the left side of the inventory screen, you will see 9 buttons. Each one loads a build.`Builds 1,2,3 are ship components. 4,5,6 are for ship devices. 7,8,9 are away team load-outs.` &16 `Each category is independent of the others.` &99 `Changing ship build (1,2,3) does not affect device builds (4,5,6) or away team builds (7,8,9). Each is tracked separately, and installing an item installs it to the currently selected build.` &18 `(Reach sector 10 to permanently unlock builds!)

You can install between 1 and 3 weapons on your ship, determined by your reactor.``Note that attacks always hit, unless the target has some rare ability to dodge or deflect.``Ship weapons fall into 3 categories: Cannons, Beams, and Missiles.``&78 Cannons &99 fire solid projectiles. They tend to have the shortest effective range, and do the same damage against shields and hull. Cannon damage is affected by the target's evasion stat, but not point defense.``&78 Beams &99 have medium range and use the least supplies. Many beams only do half damage against shields, but are unaffected by the target's evasion or point defense.``&78 Missiles &99 have the longest range and best damage, but use the most supplies. They are affected by both the target's evasion and point defense (PD). PD reduces missile damage by about 80%, but each missile strike reduces PD by the missile's 'hardness' stat.``

All ship weapons have the following stats:``&78 DM (Damage)&99  : The average amount of damage a hit from this weapon does, not counting any other factors. Note that attacks always hit, except in certain special circumstances.``&78 [DPT] (Damage Per Turn)&99  : The weapon's damage divided by its cooldown time. A weapon that does 21 damage and has a cooldown of 3 would show [7] damage per turn.``&78 RN (Range)&99  : How many tiles away the weapon can hit.``&78 CD (Cooldown)&99  : How many turns it takes for this weapon to fire again.``&78 PD (Point Defense)&99  : How much this weapon contributes to your point defense total. PD is a passive stat of all ship weapons and it protects against incoming missile damage.``&78 SU (Supply Use)&99  : How many supplies are consumed each time the weapon is fired.``&78 (Hardness*)&99  : How much the target's point defense (PD) is reduced each time this weapon hits. &99 ``&78 (Crit Chance*)&99  : The chance to score critical hits, causing other kinds of damage like killing crew or knocking out sensors. Most crits are random, but some weapons guaranted specific crits. Weapons usually need to hit the hull (not shields) to cause crits.``&78 (Tech Rating*)&99  : Components with numerical stats have a tech rating, and higher is usually (but not always) better. Tech rating is important to crafting. `&78 `* Note: &99 Hardness, Crit Chance, and Tech Rating are not shown as abbreviations, but are displayed in details in inventory, crafting, stations, and tooltips.

Shields are energy barriers that surround your ship and absorb incoming damage. They also prevent most kinds of critical hits. ``Shields have the following stats:``&78 SHE (Shield Amount)&99  : The amount of damage your shields can absorb before dropping. Once shields are down, you are vulnerable to critical hits.``&78 RCH (Recharge Amount)&99  : The number of shield points that will recharge each turn, after the cooldown period is passed.``&78 CD (Cooldown)&99  : How many turns before your shields start to recharge. Reset when taking damage. Smaller CD is better.``&78 SU (Supplies Used)&99  : How many supplies are consumed each turn your shields recharge. If you don't have enough supplies, your shields won't recharge!

Cloaking Devices make your ship invisible, and take the place of shields (you can have one or the other). Some ships can break your cloak at a certain range (displayed when tooltipping).``When your ship cloaks, all enemies lose their target lock. When shooting after 2 or 3 turns of being cloaked, your shots do either double or triple damage. 3x is the maximum multiplier.``There are 2 kinds of cloaks: Strategic and Tactical.``Tactical cloaks only work for a few turns, use supplies when activated, but their cooldown time isn't very long. They provide no shields, and have the following stats:``&78 DUR (Duration) &99 : How many turns before the cloak drops and you becomes visible again.``&78 CD (Cooldown) &99 : How many turns before it can be activated again.``&78 SU (Supplies Used) &99 : How many supplies are used when the cloak is activated.``Strategic cloaks last until dropped, use supplies every turn, and take a long time to cool down. They provide some shields, which recharge immediately when their cooldown is complete. They have the following stats:``&78 SHE (Shields)&99 : The amount of defensive shield points provided once cooldown is complete.``&78 CD (Cooldown) &99 : How many turns before it can be activated again.``&78 SU (Supplies Used) &99 : How many supplies are used per turn when the cloak is active.

Armor protects your ship from damage, but it doesn't recharge like shields: it needs to be repaired at a station.``Some kinds of armor grant special powers, like resistance to radiation or less damage from beam weapons.``Armor has the following stats:``&78 ARM (Armor) &99 : The amount of damage the armor can take before it is destroyed (yes, armor is destroyed if this is ever reduced to 0).`Note: the more base hull your ship has (view in stats screen), the stronger your armor will be (this is already accounted for in the ARM stat).``&78 SPD (Speed) &99 : How much this armor modifies your ship's total speed.

Sensors allow your ship to "see" the universe. They determine how far you can see, and how much detail you get when you scan planets or shipwrecks before landing an away team. Sensors can also affect how much damage your weapons cause, by improving your targeting.``&78 RN (Range) &99 : How far away (in tiles) your ship can see. This effects how quickly you reveal the map, and is also a hard limit on your weapons range (even with range 7 missiles, if you can only see 4 tiles, you can only *shoot* 4 tiles). Enemies can still see and shoot you too.``&78 TGT (Targeting) &99 : The percentage damage bonus or penalty all your ship weapons get, based on your sensors' ability to aim accurately (remember: attacks always hit, but damage is variable).``&78 SCN (Scanning) &99 : The amount of detail your orbital scans reveal about potential landing sites. Most planetary atmospheres reduce scanning efficiency (reported in the scan data).``

Engines allow your ship to move. That's important. ``They have the following stats:``&78 EV (Evasion) &99 : Reduces incoming damage from cannon and missile weapons by up to 85% (hard cap). &14 Negative evasion *increases* damage taken! ``&78 SPD (Speed) &99 : The modifier to your ship's total speed, which affects how often you get to move compared to other entities. Can be negative (bad) or positive (good).``&78 SU (Supplies Used) &99 : The number of supplies consumed per move in space. Your engines do not use supplies while sitting still, but your reactor does.``

Allows travel between sectors via warp points. Must recharge after use. ``They have the following stats:``&78 RN (Range) &99 : How many sectors your can warp at once (max is 99). ``&78 CD (Cooldown) &99 : How long after warping before you can warp again.``&78 SUP (Supplies Used) &99 : The number of supplies consumed when warping.``

Possibly the single most important component on your ship: it powers everything! Determines how many weapons and devices you can equip. If you get too low on supplies, crew members will start throwing stuff in the reactor to keep you going. ``Reactors have the following stats:``&78 WEP (Weapons) &99 : The number of weapons (1-3) this reactor supports. Reactors that support more weapons use more supplies per turn.``&78 DEV (Devices) &99 : The number of devices (1-6) this reactor supports. Reactors that support more devices use more supplies per turn, whether those devices are equipped or not.``&78 SPD (Speed) &99 : The modifier to your ship's overall speed. ``&78 SUP (Supplies Used) &99 : The number of supplies consumed every turn, whether you move or not.``

Every kind of away team gun and melee weapon has a special behavior. You can use these to create builds focused on offense, defense, mobility, or balance.``Ranged Weapons:``&78 Pistol (Dual Wield) &99 : With pistols in your main and swap slot, fire both each turn.`&78 Rifle (Return Fire) &99 : With a rifle in your main slot, while standing in cover, you automatically shoot back at anyone who shoots at you.`&78 Shotgun (Knockback) &99 : Shotguns hit multiple targets and forcefully knock them back.`&78 SMG (Suppression) &99 : Targets are suppressed, getting a 33% accuracy penalty for a few turns (their attacks might miss).`&78 Sniper (Range) &99 : Gives +1 vision range, but 50% chance to miss at close range (1 or 2).`&78 Blaster (Opoportunity Attack) &99 : Get a free shot at the first hostile target that moves within range per turn.`&78 Beamer (Accuracy) &99 : The beamer's shots can't be dodged (except by 1 creature with "nasty, big, pointy teeth").`&78 Cloudgun (Protection) &99 : Hits everything in its path and protects the away team from its element (fire, acid, etc.).`&78 Launcher (Boom) &99 : Hits everything in the 3x3 target area.``Melee Weapons:``&78 Knife (Auto-Attack) &99 : When moving, automatically attack any hostile creatures within range.`&78 Sword (Parry) &99 : 33% chance to block incoming melee attacks.`&78 Hammer (Slow) &99 : Knocks back and permanently slows targets.`&78 Eviscerator (Strikeback) &99 : Automatically attack the first enemy that melee attacks you each turn.`&78 Zapper (Spread) &99 : Spreads from your target, hitting all adjacent enemies.`&78 Extractor (Sample) &99 : Guaranteed to extract an essence when killing an adjacent target.`

Every away team weapon (whether ranged, melee, or grenade) has a damage type, like slashing, incendiary, or stun. ``Each weapon does one kind of damage. A shock pistol does shock damage, even though it shoots a bullet, which is normally piercing damage.``The base version of most guns do piercing damage. For melee weapons, the knife does piercing, the sword is slashing, the hammer causes blunt damage, and the eviscerator and extractor do hybrid damage. Zappers are "elemental", and cause fire, cryo, corrosive, or other more exotic damage types.``The creatures you encounter will have various resistances and vulnerabilities to certain damage types. The rock colossus is immune to slashing damage, but weak against cryo and acid. Xenocide weapons are deadly to insects and plants, but virtually useless against other creatures.``Here is a list of all currently available damage types: Piercing, Cutting, Smashing, Hybrid, Incendiary, Cryo, Explosive, Corrosive, Shock, Sonic, Scrambler, Xenocide, Disruptor, Neutron, Fear, Stun, Toxic, Ion, Plasma, Graviton, Nano, Nuclear, Tangler, Grappler.``Here are some special characteristics of certain damage types:``Explosive and corrosive damage are good at removing walls and other obstructions.`Sonic weapons require atmospheric pressure between 0.5 and 2.5 to function.`Toxic and xenocide weapons release clouds of gas that remain for several turns.`Grappler weapons can pull targets closer, and tangler can immobilize them.`Hybrid damage is rare and few creatures are resistant to it.

Ranged weapons carried by the away team. You have a main slot and a swap slot, and you can freely change between the two. Every kind of gun has a special power that is noted in its description in tooltips.``They have the following stats:``&78 DM (Damage) &99 : Base amount of damage done by this weapon. ``&78 RN (Range) &99 : How far away (in tiles) this weapon can shoot. Requires unblocked line of sight.``&78 ADJ (Adjacent Hits) &99 : Some weapons can hit additional creatures around the initial target. This is the number of additional targets hit.``&78 NOK (Knockback) &99 : A measure of the impact force of the weapon, rated 0-4. Any positive value has a chance to push the target back.``&78 SPD (Speed) &99 : The modifier to your away team's total speed. Speed is modified by both equipped guns, your melee weapon, suit, and any skills or powers. Terrain also has an effect on speed.``&78 (Damage Type) &99 : Every weapon has a damage *type* (piercing, cryo, tangler, etc.), which is part of the name and noted in the weapon's icon. There will also be a short description of the damage type in any tooltip. Creatures on away missions have a variety of resistances and vulnerabilities to different damage types, which will be displayed in tooltips if known.``

Melee weapons are for when monsters get too close. Move into a creature to attack with melee. Each melee weapon has a special power that is noted in its description in tooltips.``They have the following stats:``&78 DM (Damage) &99 : The base damage done by this weapon. It will be affected by the target's resistance or vulnerability to the weapon's damage type.``&78 SPD (Speed) &99 : The modifier to your away team's total speed. ``

Suits are used by away teams for survival in all hostile environments, don't leave the ship without one. ``They have the following stats:``&78 HP (Hit Points) &99 : The amount of damage you have to take before one member of your away team dies (crew first, then officers, then the captain, if present).``&78 OX (Oxygen) &99 : How much oxygen the suit holds, which equates to how many moves you can take before needing to refill (unless you're somewhere with breathable air, or have the "unlimited oxygen" cheat).``&78 VIS (Vision Range) &99 : How far away (in tiles) your away team can see. Helps you explore faster and notice threats. Standing on mountains can temporarily increase your vision range.``&78 ER (Enviro-Resist) &99 : Most planets cause environmental damage (frozen planets are cold (minor damage), while molten planets want to set you on fire (ouch!). Environmental resistance is how much the suit reduces that damage. When scanning a planet, you will see how much (if any) environmental damage you will take per turn there.``&78 SPD (Speed) &99 : The modifier to your away team's total speed. ``If your equipped suit doesn't already have a special power, then trying to install an away team device will give you the option of permanently upgrade that suit with that power.

Compact explosive device for throwing. Hits multiple tiles. Many types available, including explosive, incendiary, and tangler. ``They have the following stats:``&78 DM (Damage) &99 : The base damage this grenade does to all targets within its explosion radius. It will be modified by each target's resistances.`&78 `RAD (Radius) &99 : How large (in tiles) the explosion radius is, 1-3 tiles in every direction from the center.``&78 AMMO (Ammunition) &99 : How many of these grenades you have. Each grenade has a maximum. Finding grenade ammo crates allow you to carry 50% more than the intended maximum.`If you run out of ammo, this grenade item is "destroyed".``

Devices are similar to components in that they are installed in either your ship or away team in slots. But devices don't have stats, they have effects, like allowing your ship to safely enter ion storms, or letting the away team walk on the outer hull of shipwrecks.``A ship can install up to 6 devices (depending on your reactor). Most ships also have 1 or 2 permanent "built-in" devices: these can't be removed, transferred, or salvaged.``Your away team is limited to 1 device, although one can also be installed into your current space suit while you're still on the ship.``Devices can be found, bought at stations, crafted, or received as quest rewards.

Components and devices are "installed" from the inventory screen. You can't remove or replace an item that is cooling down (but your away team can still swap weapons if they're on cooldown).``When on away missions, you can't access your full inventory unless you're standing on the shuttle or airlock (or if you chose the "install anywhere" cheat at the start of your game). And no matter what cheats you have, you can only change your suit when you're safely onboard the ship!

The best thing about officers is that they have skills. Officers get 1 passive skill per level.`Some skills are used in space, some just on the away team, and others are useful everywhere.``Some skills provide bonuses like doing extra damage or seeing further.`Others provide new abilities, like walking on water or digging through walls.``Each officer can have up to 6 skills. Most skills have 2 or 3 levels.`Sometimes higher skill levels mean bigger effects, but some grant new abilities at each level.``Passive skills are automatic: you don't have to do anything to use them.``Away team skills require that the officer actually join the away team to have any effect. `Injured officers have their skills disabled, and they grant no bonus until the officer heals.``Once an officer reaches level 11, those max skill levels mean nothing, and officers can become extremely powerful. Any numerical maximums (like max speed) still apply.``For reference, most winning captains are between level 8 and 10.

The effects of skills stack with devices and artifacts, so if you have different sources of the same effect, they will add to make that effect stronger (sometimes up to a maximum).`Even 2 different officers with different skills that provide the same effect *will stack*.``But having 2 officers with the exact same skill will not stack. `There's no point in hiring 5 engineers to try to buff your crafting level.``There are a few devices that can be installed multiple times and their effects will stack: cargo containers, supply storage, and smuggler's compartment. No other devices can be multi-installed, and no other same-source effects stack.``You can see the combined effects of all skills, devices, and known artifact powers in Infinipedia => Active Effects.``You can even turn effects off there, one at a time or all at once.

Cyber-skills are activated abilities that require a cybernetic module and have a cooldown.`Each officer can equip up to 2 cyber-skills for space and 2 for away missions.``Cyber-skills are color coded by division, just like officer classes: blue, yellow, red, green, and purple. A purple officer (pathfinder or transmutor) can use purple skills but not any other.``The captain always starts with 1 cyber-skill for space, and 1 for away missions.`You need to find the rest! They are most often located in containers on shipwrecks,`but sometimes sold in stations.``Cooldowns:``When activated, cyber-skills have a cooldown time before they can be used again.`Each division has a color-coded cybernetic gel (a kind of consumable) associated with it, that cuts the cooldown time in half. Red gel cools down red skills, etc.``Use gel by activating a skill that is already cooling down, or with the "Use" command.`Using gel does not end your turn, but you can only use one gel of each color per turn.``Upgrades:``Cyber-skills can be upgraded in the "Mods" section of the Crafting menu.`Upgrading cyber-skills costs a lot of essences, but they can become very powerful.``

"Injury" is a state that disables an officer's passive skills, and sometimes active skills as well.``Officers can be injured on away missions, or by certain procedures (VR training, re-speccing, etc.).
