Diseases are rampant in the galaxy. This is believed to be due to a period of advanced biological warfare at some point in the past.``More than half of all terran planets have an endemic pathogen that can be contracted from the environment. The mutations on shipwrecks like zombies and floating eyeballs are believed to be caused by a mutagenic disease.``Therefore the use of spacesuits is common practice, even when the air is otherwise breathable.``Some creatures are natural disease carriers and any contact has a chance to infect you (this information can be seen by tooltipping the creature).``A now-defunct medical institution called the UHO (universal health organization) once conducted a microbial survey, certifying some planets as disease-free. This does not mean that creatures living there don't carry diseases. Seriously, suit up.``If you have your suit helmets open and there is a disease present, you will have a small chance of exposure every turn.

Sickness goes through several stages: Exposure, Asymptomatic, Symptomatic, and Remission.``Upon exposure, one crew member is infected. Further exposure may increase the number. If all infected crew members die or are cured before the crew returns to the ship, then all is well and the medical emergency is over. Otherwise the disease will spread.``The *if* part means that if you're ruthless enough, and the captain isn't on the away mission, you can strand infected crew and not let them return to the ship.``Diseases start as asymptomatic: this is the period when it's not actually having any effect yet. It's getting worse and possibly spreading. `&14 Space stations can't cure diseases during the asymptomatic phase.` &99 `When symptoms begin, you will get a popup alert. Your crew will start taking damage. Most diseases also have 1-5 symptoms, which are not just funny names, but bad effects. They're the opposite of skills: they make you worse at things! ``Once symptoms begin to show, you can check Infinipedia => Active Effects and look for negative effects highlighted in yellow or red. ` &16 `You can learn about your disease's symptoms by tooltipping the biohazard status effect icon on the right of the map screen.` &99 `Diseases can be cured by some space stations, though the staff at Bankers hospitals often seem to have troubles of their own. A science officer skilled in virology can also work to cure disease, but it can take a long time.``Once a disease has been "cured", it goes into remission and your people begin to recover.`Remission usually lasts 5-50 turns.`During this phase, there is still the threat of mutation (see next section).

Consider it a blessing that each planet or shipwreck only has one disease.``Why? &14 Because diseases can mutate!` &99 `If you already have a disease, and you're exposed to a different pathogen, the two will combine to become something extra-terrible.``Their damage and transmission rates will increase, and they will have new symptoms.``Mutated diseases are more expensive to cure, and the remission period lasts longer.``Repeated exposures can make problems worse with further mutations.``Get a cure!``Or better yet, try an "Immune Booster" consumable today! According to the package:`"Immune Booster Makes it nearly impossible™ for your crew to catch diseases for 300 turns."

A science officer with the virology skill (or an immunization station device) can let you treat diseases yourself automatically.``At level 1 of the skill, the officer will immediately begin work on a cure, and the percentage of completion will appear in the status icon on the right. The medical lab device also contributes to speeding up this auto-cure process.``But with level 2 of virology (or the device), you will discover a cure using rare plants! At level 3+, you'll get a second even more convoluted cure method.``These will be turned into a quest, and as soon as you have the necessary items on your ship, the disease will be instantly cured, with no remission period. On top of that, you get immunity to diseases you cure yourself!

Space is divided into sectors, and sectors are connected by warp points.`A warp point can take you to any sector within range of your warp drive. ``You can freely skip over sectors unless your warp drive only has a range of 1, and in that case, get a new one quick!.`Maximum warp range is 99 sectors in a single jump!``You can also revisit sectors, and in fact this can be very beneficial, especially for traders who want to exploit known price differences. It also means you can come back to complete an away mission once you've found a needed piece of equipment.``On the warp screen, you can see all the sectors within range of 2 warp jumps (up to 99 sectors in either direction). Scroll through available destinations with the arrow keys, the horizontal scroll bar, or even the mouse wheel.``Your current sector is a green circle, visited sectors within range are blue, unknowns are orange. Any sector that is beyond your current warp range is gray. Selecting a sector will show a gold line between your current location and the destination.``Next to the sector selector you can see a map of the galaxy and an indication of your relative place within it. The warp point network spirals slowly toward the center of the galaxy.``The bottom part of the screen shows known info about the selected sector, with a map on the right and known commodity prices in the middle. The left side lists a wealth of information about contents, inhabitants, quests, and any notes you've taken.``To warp, you must be on a warp point and your warp drive mustn't be cooling down.``

These few sectors were the last hold-out of the Terran Coalition,  a once-great stellar civilization. What happened?
The human race isn't gone, or dead, or lost. Just scattered. There is no "homeworld" anymore, no Earth. "Sanctuary Space" is a cruel joke. But they carry on, finding purpose where they can.
What great enemy laid waste to humanity's heritage? Greed. Alien avarice and mankind's materialism, feeding off of each other.
It was the greatest arms race in history, fueled by an alien mega-corporation with seemingly limitless technological advancements, doled out piecemeal to the highest bidder.
Old angers flared, rivalries renewed. Man against man, colony versus core-world. When money wasn't enough, real estate became the currency. Entire worlds were strip-mined to fund the fight.
The Bankers. They are your enemy. For now, you need them. They have the supplies and equipment you require. But bide your time. Labor to lift their yoke.
You are not alone. Not only humans`have fallen to the Bankers' interstellar operations.``Seek out allies among the other lost souls in this galaxy.`Find purpose.``Find the Resistance!
Why do you think there are so many unexplored planets? They're not "unexplored". They're just new to you. And you collect that precious data...

All you independent spacers, you sell the Bankers whatever you find, and you buy up all their scraps. They scan your ship! They never offer anything much better than you already have!
Data greases the mega-corporate meat grinder! You're leading your own people to their deaths, and then paying the bankers just so you can do it all again!
